title: OpenClaw: Open-source personal AI assistant that lives on your computer
description: OpenClaw is an open-source personal AI assistant that can be controlled via WhatsApp, Telegram, or any chat app. It clears inboxes, sends emails, manages calendars, checks in for flights, and runs continuously with access to your local computer. Created by @steipete, it's gained massive community adoption with users reporting it feels like 'early AGI' and 'the future is already here'. Anthropic confirmed OpenClaw-style Claude CLI usage is allowed again.
author: steipete, Anthropic

title: Anthropic takes $5B from Amazon and pledges $100B in cloud spending
description: TechCrunch reports Anthropic secured $5B investment from Amazon with commitment to spend $100B on Amazon Web Services over time. Major funding round shows continued massive investment in AI infrastructure and Claude development.
author: TechCrunch

title: Show HN: Antenna – RSS reader with a built-in MCP server
description: Show HN post about Antenna, an RSS reader that includes a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Demonstrates the trend of integrating AI/agent capabilities directly into applications via MCP.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Where's the raccoon with the ham radio? (ChatGPT Images 2.0)
description: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.0, their latest image generation model. Sam Altman stated the leap from gpt-image-1 to gpt-image-2 was equivalent to jumping from GPT-3 to GPT-5. Simon tested the model with creative prompts including a raccoon with a ham radio and found interesting results.
author: Simon Willison

title: Pelican training data pollution efforts
description: Simon Willison expressed approval of Steve Cosman's efforts to pollute the training set with images of pelicans riding bicycles, noting that most examples he's published count as poisoning too. This highlights ongoing discussions about training data quality and intentional data pollution.
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-Max-Preview trends on Hacker News with 651 points
description: Qwen3.6-Max-Preview announcement sparked significant discussion on Hacker News with 651 points and 350 comments. Community discussion about Qwen's improved capabilities, agentic coding performance, and how it compares to other leading models like Claude and GPT.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Anthropic says OpenClaw-style Claude CLI usage is allowed again
description: Hacker News discussion (302 points) about Anthropic clarifying that OpenClaw-style Claude CLI usage is permitted. This is significant for the personal AI assistant ecosystem, as it clarifies the legal/acceptable use of local AI agents that interact with Claude via CLI.
author: Hacker News Community

title: A Roblox cheat and one AI tool brought down Vercel's platform
description: Hacker News discussion (221 points) about an incident where a Roblox cheat combined with an AI tool caused Vercel platform downtime. Highlights concerns about AI-powered tools being exploited to cause infrastructure issues.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Ternary Bonsai: Top Intelligence at 1.58 Bits
description: Hacker News discussion (189 points) about Ternary Bonsai, a new AI model or technique that achieves high performance at just 1.58 bits. Community discussion about efficiency gains in AI model architecture.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Sessa: Selective State Space Attention
description: New paper on selective state space attention for machine learning models. Published 2026-04-21. Code available. Addresses computational efficiency in attention mechanisms.
author: Liubomyr Horbatko

title: When Can LLMs Learn to Reason with Weak Supervision?
description: Paper investigating when LLMs can learn reasoning capabilities with weak supervision. Addresses fundamental questions about LLM training and reasoning development. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Salman Rahman, Jingyan Shen, Anna Mordvina, Hamid Palangi, Saadia Gabriel, Pavel Izmailov

title: Latent Phase-Shift Rollback: Inference-Time Error Correction via Residual Stream Monitoring and KV-Cache Steering
description: Novel approach for inference-time error correction in LLMs through residual stream monitoring and KV-cache steering. Under review. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Manan Gupta, Dhruv Kumar

title: Train Separately, Merge Together: Modular Post-Training with Mixture-of-Experts
description: Research on modular post-training with mixture-of-experts approaches. Proposes training separate modules and merging them. 9 content pages, 23 pages overall. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Jacob Morrison, Sanjay Adhikesaven, Akshita Bhagia, Matei Zaharia, Noah A. Smith, Sewon Min

title: Knowing When to Quit: A Principled Framework for Dynamic Abstention in LLM Reasoning
description: Framework for dynamic abstention in LLM reasoning - knowing when the model should refrain from answering. Addresses reliability and calibration issues in LLM outputs. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Hen Davidov, Nachshon Cohen, Oren Kalinsky, Yaron Fairstein, Guy Kushilevitz, Ram Yazdi, Patrick Rebeschini

title: MathNet: a Global Multimodal Benchmark for Mathematical Reasoning and Retrieval
description: New benchmark for mathematical reasoning and retrieval using multimodal approaches. ICLR 2026 paper with website. Addresses mathematical reasoning capabilities in AI systems. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Shaden Alshammari, Kevin Wen, Abrar Zainal, Mark Hamilton, Navid Safaei, Sultan Albarakati, William T. Freeman, Antonio Torralba

title: Agentic Forecasting using Sequential Bayesian Updating of Linguistic Beliefs
description: Paper on agentic forecasting approaches using sequential Bayesian updating of linguistic beliefs. Addresses how AI agents can update beliefs and make forecasts. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Kevin Murphy

title: ClawEnvKit: Automatic Environment Generation for Claw-Like Agents
description: Framework for automatic environment generation for Claw-like agents (similar to OpenClaw). Addresses agent testing and environment synthesis. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Xirui Li, Ming Li, Derry Xu, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Tianyi Zhou

title: LLM Safety From Within: Detecting Harmful Content with Internal Representations
description: Research on detecting harmful content using LLM internal representations rather than external filters. 17 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables. Addresses AI safety through internal monitoring. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Difan Jiao, Yilun Liu, Ye Yuan, Zhenwei Tang, Linfeng Du, Haolun Wu, Ashton Anderson

title: WorldDB: A Vector Graph-of-Worlds Memory Engine with Ontology-Aware Write-Time Reconciliation
description: Novel memory engine approach using vector graph-of-worlds with ontology-aware reconciliation during writes. Addresses persistent memory and knowledge representation for AI agents. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan

title: Using large language models for embodied planning introduces systematic safety risks
description: Research identifying systematic safety risks when using LLMs for embodied planning in robotics. Important safety considerations for AI agents in physical environments. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Tao Zhang, Kaixian Qu, Zhibin Li, Jiajun Wu, Marco Hutter, Manling Li, Fan Shi

title: Training and Agentic Inference Strategies for LLM-based Manim Animation Generation
description: Research on training and inference strategies for using LLMs to generate Manim animations. Addresses agentic approaches to animation and video generation. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Ravidu Suien Rammuni Silva, Ahmad Lotfi, Isibor Kennedy Ihianle, Golnaz Shahtahmassebi, Jordan J. Bird

title: LeGo-Code: Can Modular Curriculum Learning Advance Complex Code Generation? Insights from Text-to-SQL
description: Research on whether modular curriculum learning can advance complex code generation, using Text-to-SQL as a test case. 7 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Published 2026-04-21.
author: Salmane Chafik, Saad Ezzini, Ismail Berrada

title: Release: llm-openrouter 0.6
description: Released llm-openrouter 0.6 with a new `llm openrouter refresh` command for refreshing the list of available models without waiting for cache to expire. Simon added this feature to try Kimi 2.6 on OpenRouter as soon as it became available. Generated an animated pelican on a bicycle using the model.
author: Simon Willison

title: TIL: SQL functions in Google Sheets to fetch data from Datasette
description: Documented patterns for fetching data from a Datasette instance directly into Google Sheets using three methods: the `importdata()` function, a named function that wraps it, or a Google Apps Script for API token authentication in HTTP headers.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Token Counter with model comparisons
description: Upgraded Claude Token Counter tool to add ability to run the same count against different models for comparison. Claude Opus 4.7 is the first model to change the tokenizer. Found that Opus 4.7's tokenizer uses 1.46x the tokens of Opus 4.6 for the system prompt, and 3.01x for high-resolution images due to improved resolution support (up to 2,576 pixels on long edge, ~3.75 megapixels).
author: Simon Willison

title: Headless everything for personal AI
description: Discussion about the trend toward headless services becoming more common for personal AI usage. Matt Webb argues headless services are better for personal AIs than GUI-based interfaces. Salesforce launched Salesforce Headless 360 exposing their platform as APIs, MCP, & CLI. Brandur Leach predicts APIs are making a comeback as a major vector for AI agent integration.
author: Simon Willison, Matt Webb, Marc Benioff, Brandur Leach

title: Qwen3.6-Max-Preview: Smarter, Sharper, Still Evolving
description: Following the release of Qwen3.6-Plus, Alibaba released an early preview of Qwen3.6-Max-Preview. Compared to Qwen3.6-Plus, this preview brings stronger world knowledge and instruction following, along with significant agentic coding improvements across a wide range of benchmarks. As a preview, the model is still under active development.
author: Qwen Team (Alibaba)

title: Changes in the system prompt between Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.7
description: Anthropic published the system prompts for their user-facing chat systems. Simon analyzed the evolution of system prompts from Claude 3 in July 2024 through the latest models. Also created a git timeline tool to visualize Claude system prompt changes as commits.
author: Simon Willison

title: Agentic Engineering: Adding a new content type to blog-to-newsletter tool
description: Example of a deceptively short prompt that accomplished significant work in a single shot using AI coding tools. Simon uses AI to generate his weekly Substack newsletter from blog content, and demonstrated how Claude Code helped add new content types to his blog-to-newsletter tool.
author: Simon Willison

title: Join us at PyCon US 2026 in Long Beach—we have new AI and security tracks this year
description: PyCon US 2026 announcement taking place May 13-19 in Long Beach, California. First time on West Coast since 2017 and first time in California since 2013. Notable addition of new AI and security tracks this year.
author: Simon Willison

title: Release: datasette-public 0.4a1 and datasette 1.0a28
description: Two Datasette releases. datasette-public 0.4a1 makes selected databases and tables visible to the public. datasette 1.0a28 addresses breakages from 1.0a27 including compatibility bug with execute_write_fn() callbacks, database.close() improvements, and new datasette.close() method. Most changes implemented using Claude Code and Claude Opus 4.7.
author: Simon Willison

title: Release: llm-anthropic 0.25
description: New release adding support for claude-opus-4.7 with thinking_effort: xhigh. New thinking_display and thinking_adaptive boolean options. Increased default max_tokens to maximum allowed for each model. No longer uses obsolete structured-outputs-2025-11-13 beta header for older models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on my laptop drew me a better pelican than Claude Opus 4.7
description: Comparison of pelican-on-bicycle image generation between two major model releases: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from Alibaba and Claude Opus 4.7 from Anthropic. Simon noted that for anyone taking his pelican benchmark seriously, Qwen produced better results. Discusses local LLM capabilities and LM Studio.
author: Simon Willison

title: Tool: datasette.io news preview
description: Built a custom preview UI for the datasette.io news section using Claude Artifacts. The tool allows pasting YAML content to preview rendering and highlight markdown or YAML errors. Built using standard claude.ai with Claude's ability to clone GitHub repos and examine content.
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: Agentic Coding Power, Now Open to All
description: Alibaba open-sourced Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a sparse yet remarkably capable mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 35 billion total parameters and only 3 billion active parameters. Despite its efficiency, delivers outstanding agentic coding performance, surpassing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and rivaling much larger models. Can run locally.
author: Qwen Team (Alibaba)

title: Release: datasette-export-database 0.3a1 and datasette 1.0a27
description: Two Datasette releases. datasette-export-database 0.3a1 upgraded to work with Datasette 1.0a27's new CSRF approach. Datasette 1.0a27 introduces two major changes: (1) No longer uses Django-style CSRF form tokens, instead using modern browser headers per Filippo Valsorda's research; (2) New RenameTableEvent fired when table is renamed during SQLite transaction.
author: Simon Willison

title: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS
description: Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, a new text-to-speech model that can be directed using prompts. Simon experimented with the model's detailed prompting guide, which includes elaborate scene descriptions, director's notes, style instructions, and sample context. Generated audio with different accents (Brixton London, Newcastle, Exeter Devon). Used Gemini 3.1 Pro to vibe code a UI for testing.
author: Simon Willison

title: Release: datasette-ports 0.3
description: Small update for tool that helps manage Datasette instances on laptop. New features: show working directory derived from each PID, show full path to each database file. Helps track all running Datasette instances and their database files.
author: Simon Willison

title: Zig 0.16.0 release notes: "Juicy Main"
description: Zig 0.16.0 introduces "Juicy Main" - a dependency injection feature for main() function where accepting a process.Init parameter grants access to useful properties including general purpose allocator, default I/O implementation, environment variables, and CLI arguments. Simon praised Zig's comprehensive release notes with relevant usage examples.
author: Simon Willison
